To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) men and women evaluate cooperative partners and their entitlements to spoils differently, (2) productivity is valued more than generosity, but generosity is valued more than productivity, (3) generosity is valued more in skilled partners than in lucky partners, (4) men value productivity more than women, and (5) generosity is valued by both sexes more than the game's incentive structure predicts.

the evaluation of a cooperative partner’s productivity and generosity cannot fully be explained by the incentive structures of the games, but appear calibrated for choosing long-term cooperative partners and dividing resources in a biological market.
